definition: Organoid intelligence (OI) is an emerging field of study in computer science and biology that develops and studies biological wetware computing using 3D cultures of human brain cells (or brain organoids) and brain-machine interface technologies.
details: Such technologies may be referred to as OIs or the nervous filesystem. Organoid intelligent computer systems can be an example of biohybrid systems.

explainer.lead: Organoid intelligence is an emerging field that develops biological wetware computing using 3D cultures of human brain cells, or brain organoids, together with brain-machine interface technologies. It matters as an example of biohybrid systems combining biology and computing.

tiers.eli5: Instead of building chips, researchers grow small clusters of brain cells and try to use them as a computing material.
tiers.practitioner: The field studies 3D cultures of human brain cells alongside brain-machine interface technologies; such systems may be called OIs or the nervous filesystem. A pitfall is that this is an emerging field rather than an established engineering practice.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as an emerging field of computer science and biology developing biological wetware computing using 3D cultures of human brain cells (brain organoids) and brain-machine interface technologies, an example of biohybrid systems.

explainer.example: A 3D culture of human brain cells connected through brain-machine interface technology is studied as a biohybrid computing system.
